title: Signal Telescope: Raw-to-Ops Playbook (Apr 2026)
content:
Context and intent:
This is a lightweight working playbook for turning recent field signals into ops actions and small exploratory feature deliveries. Purpose: speed (48–72h micropatches), clarity (single owner per thread), and signal hygiene (capture quotes + telemetry pointers). Not a roadmap — tactical triage to reduce customer friction quickly and surface higher-impact asks to product.

Data sources used:
- Recent support threads (top 25 by latency impact, Mar–Apr 2026)
- Pilot account interviews (3 enterprise, 4 mid-market) run by Solutions Eng (notes linked)
- Telemetry hooks: token-cost spikes, model-fallback frequency, request error bursts (see linked JIRA)
- Slack escalations (cs-escalations channel)

High-level synthesis (one-paragraph):
Customers consistently call out three patterns: (1) unpredictable cost spikes when using long-context chat sessions (esp. with embeddings+gen workflows), (2) surprise model fallbacks when Dedicated pools spike and the routing policy silently selects smaller variants, causing functional regressions, and (3) lack of quick observability for per-route prefix caching stats (teams cannot tell whether caching is active or ineffective). These lead to user-facing latency regressions, billing disputes, and repeated guardrail requests.

Representative customer vignettes (redacted):
- "We saw our costs jump 3x after a weekend run — we couldn't tell which routes or prompts caused it." — Large marketplace platform
- "Our chat flows sometimes return older model behavior during busy hours; model changes break our tests." — Fintech analytics team
- "We try to tune prefix cache but have zero visibility into hit rates, so we're guessing." — Healthcare POC lead

Quick-win micropatch candidates (48–72h):
1) Per-route caching dashboard card (UX + 1 backend metric): show last 7-day hit rate + recent evictions. Owner: Liam. Effort: small backend metric + console card. Expected impact: reduces guesswork and support tickets.
2) Fallback audible log: when a request falls back to a lower-tier model, emit a short flag in the response (header) and a brief event in the request trace. Owner: Diego. Effort: small runtime flag + trace plumbing. Expected impact: immediate debugging improvement for customers seeing silent regressions.
3) Cost spike alert template: create a default Kibana alert tied to high 1h token variance across top N routes. Owner: Maya. Effort: config + runbook. Expected impact: faster incident detection and reduced billing disputes.

Priority feature requests (synthesized, with impact/effort triage):
- Request: "Explicit routing preview for canary & traffic splits"
  - Why: customers need to validate that traffic will follow pinned model variants during rollouts.
  - Impact: high (prevents regressions at rollout time).
  - Effort: medium (console + simulation service).
  - Suggested MVP: a preview simulator showing percentile latency/cost delta for a candidate route. Owner: product-hosted-api.

- Request: "Granular cost attribution by prompt-set"
  - Why: finance teams want to attribute charges to feature owners rather than broad routes.
  - Impact: high for enterprise billing reconciliation.
  - Effort: medium-high (instrumentation + billing pipeline changes).
  - Suggested MVP: attach lightweight tags to requests and expose a tagged spend dashboard. Owner: finance-eng collateral.

- Request: "Deterministic fallback policies (no silent model downgrade)"
  - Why: unpredictability in fallbacks breaks correctness-sensitive workflows.
  - Impact: high for regulated customers.
  - Effort: high (runtime + policy UI).
  - Suggested MVP: an opt-in strict routing toggle that rejects requests rather than fallback. Owner: serving-runtime + product.

Proposed experiments (2-week horizons):
- Experiment A: Prefix-cache guidance A/B test. Roll out an in-console prompt that suggests cache TTLs and shows expected token-savings for a sample workload. Measurement: change in cache hit rate + per-route token cost delta after 2 weeks. Owner: Optimize team.
- Experiment B: Canary traffic preview with synthetic replay. Allow customers to run a small replay of last N requests against candidate variants; measure divergence in outputs. Measurement: number of prevented regressions during subsequent live rollout. Owner: Console and Release Eng.

Runbook snippets (what to do when a signal arrives):
1) Triage (owner within 24h): capture first-response summary, attach sample request(s), link telemetry, add label 'signal_telescope'.
2) Quick-fix eval (48–72h): can this be resolved with a micropatch (dashboard card, header flag, alert)? If yes, schedule immediate small PR.
3) Escalate (if >3 customers impacted or regulatory surface): open JIRA with severity P2/P1, notify SRE and runtime leads, and schedule cross-team sync.

Owner map for current threads (examples):
- Prefix-cache visibility: Liam Chen (cs -> console): follow-up with console PO for prototype card.
- Silent fallbacks: Diego Morales (cs -> runtime): capture two repro cases and request trace-level flag.
- Cost spikes runbook: Maya Singh (cs): write template alert and publish in ops playbook.

Communication plan for customers impacted by micropatches:
- Draft a short note to be sent via support saying: "We made an update to surface X in the Console / Response header. If you continue to see Y, please reply and we'll escalate." Keep copy short, link to a playbook doc. Owner: CS communications.

Open questions and unknowns:
- Which routes produce the worst token-variance signals? Need a prioritized list from telemetry (ask infra for top-50 by spike frequency).
- How many customers would opt into strict routing vs prefer silent fallback? (Survey/CS outreach needed).
- Billing pipeline constraints for per-prompt tagging — finance/infra sync required to validate feasibility.

Appendix: Useful telemetry pointers (for engineering)
- Metric names: token_cost.per_route, fallback.count_by_variant, cache.evictions_per_min (placeholders; infra to confirm exact names).
- Quick query examples: sum(token_cost) by route over 1h windows, top 10 routes by variance.
- Slack hooks: #cs-escalations, #ops-notify.

Next steps (this doc's immediate plan):
- Share with Console PO and Serving Runtime by EOD Apr 12.
- Kick off two 72h micropatches (cache card + fallback header) with owners assigned.
- CS to audit top-10 spike routes and paste list into JIRA-CS-2147 for prioritization.

Notes to self / TODOs (short-hand)
- get sample request payloads from Support (ticket IDs included in JIRA).
- Draft outbound support template.
- Schedule 30-min cross-team huddle Fri Apr 16.

End of playbook.
